sub_branches.concept: Foundational Principles & Key Narrative of 12.1 Definition, Price Determination & Market Types
details: A market brings buyers and sellers together
Price is the mutually agreed amount
Price mechanics: High price -> low demand/surplus; Low price -> high demand/shortage; Equilibrium price satisfies both
Market types: Physical (haats, shops, malls), Online (e-commerce apps/aggregators), Domestic (within country), International (imports/exports), Wholesale, and Retail.
evidence_or_examples: Epigraph Quote - Adam Smith (18th Century Economist): Prosperity emanates from the market that develops when people need goods and services they can't create themselves.

branches.theme: 12.2 Supply Chain: Surat Textile Hub Case Study

sub_branches.concept: Foundational Principles & Key Narrative of 12.2 Supply Chain: Surat Textile Hub Case Study
details: Surat is Asia's oldest textile hub and diamond polishing center (1.5M artisans)
Physical supply chain: Raw Cotton Farmers -> Mills/Producers -> Wholesalers & Cold Storage/Warehouses -> Distributors -> Retailers -> Consumers
Online supply chain: Manufacturers -> E-commerce Aggregator Warehouses -> Doorstep Delivery.
evidence_or_examples: Margin Definition - Aggregator & Wholesaler: Aggregator combines offers from multiple sellers on an app. Wholesalers buy bulk quantities from manufacturers.

sub_branches.concept: Foundational Principles & Key Narrative of 12.3 Government Role & Quality Certification Standards
details: Government intervenes to prevent exploitation: 1
Ceiling Prices (MRP on essential medicines)
Floor Prices (MSP for agricultural crops)
Environmental Regulations (banning single-use plastics)
Provision of Public Goods (parks, roads)
Quality assessment: Checking packaging details (Net weight, MRP, Expiry/Mfg date, FSSAI lic, BEE Star ratings, ISI mark).
evidence_or_examples: Historical Precedent - Kautilya's Manasrava Rule: Arthashastra required ghee sellers to add 1/50th extra quantity (manasrava) to compensate for ghee sticking to measuring cans.

sub_branches.concept: To inspect commercial food packaging for mandatory consumer safety and quality information.
details: Locate and verify mandatory fields: Net Quantity, Mfg Date, Best Before/Expiry Date, MRP.
Check for FSSAI License Number, Allergen Declaration, Ingredients list, Nutrition Facts panel.
Inspect for presence of government certification logos.
evidence_or_examples: Observations: Mandatory packaging labels protect consumers from adulteration, short-weighting, and expired goods.
Conclusion: Mandatory packaging labels protect consumers from adulteration, short-weighting, and expired goods.

sub_branches.concept: Types of Markets and Their Characteristics
details: Physical Market | Requires physical presence of buyers and sellers | Weekly Haats, Malls, Grocery Stores
Online Market | Virtual transaction via apps/websites | E-commerce aggregators (doorstep delivery)
Wholesale Market | Deals in bulk quantities for resale | Grains Mandis, Khari Baoli Spice Market
Retail Market | Sells smaller quantities directly for final consumption | Neighborhood Kirana store
International Market | Goods/services flow across national borders | Exporting Surat diamonds to Europe

details: Price is determined at the equilibrium point where the quantity demanded by buyers matches the quantity supplied by sellers.
MSP = Minimum guaranteed price set by govt to protect farmers. MRP = Maximum Retail Price legally chargeable to consumers.
evidence_or_examples: Example/Application: Govt MSP for wheat; MRP printed on food packets

details: Q: Why did the price crash to ₹1/kg? -> A: Extreme excess supply relative to local market demand.

Q: What measures can prevent such wastage? -> A: Establishing food processing units (tomato puree/ketchup factories), expanding cold storage warehouses, and government procurement/inter-state transport distribution.
evidence_or_examples: During tomato harvest season in Andhra Pradesh, farmers produce massive surpluses. Prices drop to ₹1/kg, leading farmers to dump tomatoes on highways because transport costs exceed sales revenue.

sub_branches.concept: Comprehensive Synthesis: Explain the role of intermediaries (wholesalers, distributors, retailers) in the supply chain of physical markets.
details: 1. Manufacturers produce goods in massive bulk but cannot sell single pieces to millions of individuals. 2. Wholesalers buy bulk stocks from factories, storing them in godowns/cold storages and absorbing storage risks. 3. Distributors transport goods across difficult geographies to regional markets. 4. Retailers purchase smaller stocks from wholesalers and stock Kirana shops near residential areas, offering final consumers convenient access, credit, and variety.
